TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi.
4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency.
5. Woman is a person of female sex.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the Country or between Countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually.
11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and/or fainting and/or cause of death.
12. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery.
15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual body organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency.
17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community.
18. Transfer is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place.
19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment.
20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination.
22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred.
23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in an effort to strengthen the victim psychologically.
25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics.
26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process.
27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved.
29. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance.
32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree.
33. Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women;
34. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms.
35. Community institution is an institution formed by members of the Indonesian citizen community voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, which consists of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations.
36. Companion institution is an institution that provides assistance to women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons in Banyuwangi Regency.
37. Empathy is a mental condition that makes a person feel themselves to be in the same state of feeling or thought as the person or group who is a victim of violence and trafficking in persons.

REGENT OF BANYUWANGI
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANYUWANGI REGENCY
NUMBER 1 OF 2011
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE AND HUMAN TRAFFICKING

6.12.text:
I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children, including human trafficking, has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to education level, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection to social status, religion and beliefs, as well as particular ethnic groups, ethnicities, or races. One of the causes among them is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and human trafficking (trafficking) that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that the cases recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions on acts of trafficking of women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus, it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking as well as ensure the implementation of regional government obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

Article 9
(1) The system of organizing protection for victims of human trafficking and violence against women and children is carried out through 2 (two) methods, namely:
a. Preventive method or prevention; and
b. Repressive method or handling
(2) The preventive method or prevention is carried out through various forms of protection, both by the community and the government, which is intended to prevent the occurrence of criminal acts of human trafficking and violence or victims of violence against women and children.
(3) The repressive method or handling is carried out through various forms of protection conducted by the government through regulatory activities, implementation and enforcement of laws and regulations governing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking.
(4) The Guidelines and Technical Procedures for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking shall be further regulated through a Regent Regulation.

Article 20
(1) In implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and human trafficking, the district government may cooperate with international institutions.
(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 22
(1) Facilitation and provision of services as referred to in Article 21 letter c, in the form of victim identification, legal assistance, medical rehabilitation, psychosocial rehabilitation, social reintegration, repatriation assistance, or other forms.
(2) Facilitation and provision of services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided for women and children victims of violence including victims of trafficking in persons, women and children in conflict-prone and disaster areas, women and child workers, elderly women, women and children with disabilities, women and children victims of sexual exploitation, women heads of households, and women and children of other vulnerable groups.

TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi.
4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency.
5. Woman is a person of female sex.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the Country or between Countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually.
11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and/or fainting and/or cause of death.
12. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery.
15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual body organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency.
17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community.
18. Transfer is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place.
19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment.
20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination.
22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred.
23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in an effort to strengthen the victim psychologically.
25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics.
26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process.
27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved.
29. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance.
32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree.
33. Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women;
34. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms.
35. Community institution is an institution formed by members of the Indonesian citizen community voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, which consists of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations.
36. Companion institution is an institution that provides assistance to women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons in Banyuwangi Regency.
37. Empathy is a mental condition that makes a person feel themselves to be in the same state of feeling or thought as the person or group who is a victim of violence and trafficking in persons.

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Part One
Obligations and Responsibilities of Regional Government

Article 9
(1) The system of organizing protection for victims of human trafficking and violence against women and children is carried out through 2 (two) methods, namely:
a. Preventive method or prevention; and
b. Repressive method or handling
(2) The preventive method or prevention is carried out through various forms of protection, both by the community and the government, which is intended to prevent the occurrence of criminal acts of human trafficking and violence or victims of violence against women and children.
(3) The repressive method or handling is carried out through various forms of protection conducted by the government through regulatory activities, implementation and enforcement of laws and regulations governing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking.
(4) The Guidelines and Technical Procedures for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking shall be further regulated through a Regent Regulation.

FUNDING
Article 27
All funds required for protection activities for women and children victims of violence/human trafficking, including their recovery process, shall be charged to the Regional Budget (APBD) of Banyuwangi Regency, as well as other legitimate and non-binding revenues.

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children, including human trafficking, has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to education level, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection to social status, religion and beliefs, as well as particular ethnic groups, ethnicities, or races. One of the causes among them is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and human trafficking (trafficking) that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that the cases recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions on acts of trafficking of women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus, it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking as well as ensure the implementation of regional government obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

15. CHAPTER X
FUNDING
Article 27
All funds required for protection activities for women and children victims of violence/human trafficking, including their recovery process, shall be charged to the Regional Budget (APBD) of Banyuwangi Regency, as well as other legitimate and non-binding revenues.

I. GENERAL EXPLANATION
The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children, including human trafficking, has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to education level, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection to social status, religion and beliefs, as well as particular ethnic groups, ethnicities, or races. One of the causes among them is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and human trafficking (trafficking) that has been occurring is like the iceberg theory, meaning that the cases recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and Jaringan Penanggulangan Anak Indonesia (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, Regional Governments also have the obligation and responsibility to prevent and impose sanctions on acts of trafficking of women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, recovery and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus, it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal foundation for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking as well as ensure the implementation of regional government obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

Article 17
(1) The integration of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons shall be incorporated into planning and budget documents which include the Regional Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPD), Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD), Strategic Plan of Regional Work Units (Renstra SKPD), Regional Government Work Plan (RKPD), and Work Plan and Budget of Regional Work Units (RKA-SKPD) and related SKPD RKA.
(2) The preparation of planning and budget documents as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be harmonized among related Regional Work Units (SKPD).
(3) The SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A shall facilitate the integration of policies, programs, and activities for empowerment, protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons into the preparation of planning and budget documents as set forth in paragraph (1).
(4) In implementing as referred to in paragraph (3), the SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A shall coordinate with the Regional Development Planning Agency.

TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi.
4. SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency.
5. Woman is a person of female sex.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the Country or between Countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually.
11. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and/or fainting and/or cause of death.
12. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
14. Victim is a woman including female workers who work abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery.
15. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual body organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and indecency.
17. Recruitment is an action that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community.
18. Transfer is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place.
19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people who are their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment.
20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination.
22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred.
23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in an effort to strengthen the victim psychologically.
25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics.
26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process.
27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence.
28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved.
29. Restitution is payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs.
30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance.
32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree.
33. Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women;
34. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms.
35. Community institution is an institution formed by members of the Indonesian citizen community voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, which consists of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations.
36. Companion institution is an institution that provides assistance to women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons in Banyuwangi Regency.
37. Empathy is a mental condition that makes a person feel themselves to be in the same state of feeling or thought as the person or group who is a victim of violence and trafficking in persons.
